fr: Mon oncle habite un grand village.
en: My uncle lives in a large village.
ipa: /mɔ̃.n‿ɔ̃kl a.bit œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ vi.laʒ/
notes: Oncle and un both carry nasal vowels but with different sounds, on versus un; keep them distinct when writing.

fr: Le vin blanc est dans le verre.
en: The white wine is in the glass.
ipa: /lə vɛ̃ blɑ̃ ɛ dɑ̃ lə vɛʁ/
notes: Vin uses the in nasal sound while blanc and dans use the an nasal sound; beginners often blend the two.

fr: Ses parents arrivent demain matin.
en: Her parents arrive tomorrow morning.
ipa: /se pa.ʁɑ̃ a.ʁiv də.mɛ̃ ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Ses sounds exactly like ces and c'est; here it is the possessive ses because the parents belong to someone.

fr: Le pain chaud sent très bon.
en: The warm bread smells very good.
ipa: /lə pɛ̃ ʃo sɑ̃ tʁɛ bɔ̃/
notes: Pain and bon end the sentence with two distinct nasal vowels, in and on, that must not be swapped in spelling.

fr: Ma mère habite près de la mer.
en: My mother lives near the sea.
ipa: /ma mɛʁ a.bit pʁɛ də la mɛʁ/
notes: Mère (mother) and mer (sea) are perfect homophones; only the accent and meaning tell them apart in writing.

fr: Le bateau flotte sur l'eau calme.
en: The boat floats on the calm water.
ipa: /lə ba.to flɔt syʁ lo kalm/
notes: Bateau and eau both use the closed o sound spelled with the letters eau, not a simple o.

fr: Le roi choisit une robe noire.
en: The king chooses a black dress.
ipa: /lə ʁwa ʃwa.zi yn ʁɔb nwaʁ/
notes: Roi, choisit, and noire all spell the wa sound with oi; resist writing it as oa or wa.

fr: Sa tante attend son train à midi.
en: His aunt is waiting for her train at noon.
ipa: /sa tɑ̃t a.tɑ̃ sɔ̃ tʁɛ̃ a mi.di/
notes: Tante and attend both carry the an nasal sound while train ends in the in nasal sound; listen closely before choosing an or in.

fr: Ils sont partis très tôt ce matin.
en: They left very early this morning.
ipa: /il sɔ̃ paʁ.ti tʁɛ to sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Sont (are) sounds identical to son (his or her); here the verb form sont is required, not the possessive.

fr: Mon cœur bat vite après le jeu.
en: My heart beats fast after the game.
ipa: /mɔ̃ kœʁ ba vit a.pʁɛ lə ʒø/
notes: Cœur uses the open œu sound while jeu uses the closed eu sound, even though both come from the same two letters reversed.

fr: Tu bois beaucoup de jus d'orange.
en: You drink a lot of orange juice.
ipa: /ty bwa bo.ku də ʒy dɔ.ʁɑ̃ʒ/
notes: Tu and jus use the tight u sound while beaucoup uses the ou sound; these two vowels are easy to mix up by ear.

fr: Le vent souffle fort sur la colline.
en: The wind blows hard on the hill.
ipa: /lə vɑ̃ suf fɔʁ syʁ la kɔ.lin/
notes: Vent ends in a silent t that beginners often try to pronounce; only the nasal an vowel is actually heard.

fr: Le maire habite dans une grande maison.
en: The mayor lives in a big house.
ipa: /lə mɛʁ a.bit dɑ̃.z‿yn ɡʁɑ̃d mɛ.zɔ̃/
notes: Maire (mayor) is a homophone of mère (mother) and mer (sea); only meaning tells you which spelling fits.

fr: Cinq enfants chantent dans la cour.
en: Five children are singing in the courtyard.
ipa: /sɛ̃k ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ʃɑ̃t dɑ̃ la kuʁ/
notes: Cinq opens with the in nasal sound while enfants and chantent use the an nasal sound; the number and the verb ending must not blend.

fr: Le vert de ses yeux est magnifique.
en: The green of her eyes is magnificent.
ipa: /lə vɛʁ də se zjø ɛ ma.ɲi.fik/
notes: Vert (green) sounds just like vers (toward) and verre (glass); here it means the color.

fr: L'eau du robinet est très froide.
en: The tap water is very cold.
ipa: /lo dy ʁɔ.bi.nɛ ɛ tʁɛ fʁwad/
notes: L'eau elides the article before a vowel sound, so the article's own vowel disappears into the apostrophe rather than being written out.

fr: Mon copain aime beaucoup le pain complet.
en: My friend really loves whole wheat bread.
ipa: /mɔ̃ kɔ.pɛ̃ ɛm bo.ku lə pɛ̃ kɔ̃.plɛ/
notes: Copain and pain both spell the in nasal sound with ain, but complet ends with the on nasal sound; do not confuse the two.

fr: Le coup lui a fait mal au cou.
en: The blow hurt his neck.
ipa: /lə ku lɥi a fɛ mal o ku/
notes: Coup (blow) and cou (neck) are perfect homophones sharing the same ou sound; only meaning tells you which one to write.

fr: Je regarde le petit chat dans le jardin.
en: I am watching the little cat in the garden.
ipa: /ʒə ʁə.ɡaʁd lə pə.ti ʃa dɑ̃ lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃/
notes: Je, regarde, le, and petit all contain the light e muet sound that is often dropped in speech but must still be written.

fr: Son grand frère travaille en ville.
en: Her big brother works in the city.
ipa: /sɔ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ fʁɛʁ tʁa.vaj ɑ̃ vil/
notes: Son and grand share nasal vowels from two different families, on and an, and en here also uses the an sound rather than in.

fr: Elle voit trois oiseaux dans le ciel.
en: She sees three birds in the sky.
ipa: /ɛl vwa tʁwa.z‿wa.zo dɑ̃ lə sjɛl/
notes: Voit, trois, and oiseaux all spell the wa sound with the letters oi, a pattern that never changes.

fr: Elle a payé cent euros pour ce sac.
en: She paid one hundred euros for this bag.
ipa: /ɛl a pɛ.je sɑ̃.t‿ø.ʁo puʁ sə sak/
notes: Cent (hundred) is a homophone of sang (blood) and sans (without); context confirms the number here.

fr: Le chien a très faim ce soir.
en: The dog is very hungry tonight.
ipa: /lə ʃjɛ̃ a tʁɛ fɛ̃ sə swaʁ/
notes: Chien and faim both end in the same in nasal sound despite very different spellings, ien and aim.

fr: Ma sœur mange un œuf à la coque.
en: My sister is eating a soft-boiled egg.
ipa: /ma sœʁ mɑ̃ʒ œ̃.n‿œf a la kɔk/
notes: Sœur and œuf both use the open œu sound spelled oeu, though it looks like it should rhyme with jeu.

fr: La roue de la voiture est cassée.
en: The wheel of the car is broken.
ipa: /la ʁu də la vwa.tyʁ ɛ ka.se/
notes: Roue uses the ou sound while voiture and cassée use the u sound; these two vowels are easy to swap by ear.

fr: Il est arrivé et elle est partie.
en: He arrived and she left.
ipa: /il ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve e ɛl ɛ paʁ.ti/
notes: Est (is) and et (and) sound almost identical but never take the same spelling; only grammar tells them apart.

fr: Les enfants comptent jusqu'à cent.
en: The children count to one hundred.
ipa: /le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ kɔ̃t ʒys.ka sɑ̃/
notes: Comptent hides the nasal on sound before a silent p, while cent uses the an nasal sound spelled a different way again.

fr: Nos voisines sont arrivées avant nous.
en: Our female neighbors arrived before us.
ipa: /no vwa.zin sɔ̃.t‿a.ʁi.ve a.vɑ̃ nu/
notes: Arrivées adds a silent e and s for agreement with the feminine plural subject voisines, changing the spelling without changing the sound.

fr: Un bon vin blanc accompagne ce plat.
en: A good white wine goes with this dish.
ipa: /œ̃ bɔ̃ vɛ̃ blɑ̃ a.kɔ̃.paɲ sə pla/
notes: This short sentence packs four different nasal vowels, un, on, in, and an, each spelled its own way.

fr: Le seau tombe dans l'eau du puits.
en: The bucket falls into the well water.
ipa: /lə so tɔ̃b dɑ̃ lo dy pɥi/
notes: Seau and eau both spell the same closed o vowel with a three-letter group that gives no clue from how it looks.

fr: Ça sent bon dans sa cuisine.
en: It smells good in her kitchen.
ipa: /sa sɑ̃ bɔ̃ dɑ̃ sa kɥi.zin/
notes: Ça (that) and sa (her or his) are homophones pronounced identically; grammar alone decides which spelling fits.

fr: Mon voisin joue du piano chaque matin.
en: My neighbor plays the piano every morning.
ipa: /mɔ̃ vwa.zɛ̃ ʒu dy pja.no ʃak ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Voisin and matin both end in the in nasal sound though the letters before it differ, sin and tin.

fr: Il pleut depuis deux heures déjà.
en: It has been raining for two hours already.
ipa: /il plø də.pɥi dø.z‿œʁ de.ʒa/
notes: Pleut and deux use the closed eu sound while heures uses the open eu sound before r; the same letters shift sound depending on what follows.

fr: Ils font leurs devoirs avant le dîner.
en: They do their homework before dinner.
ipa: /il fɔ̃ lœʁ də.vwaʁ a.vɑ̃ lə di.ne/
notes: Font (do or make) sounds the same as fond (bottom); here the verb faire gives font, not the noun.

fr: Sans argent, on ne peut rien acheter.
en: Without money, one cannot buy anything.
ipa: /sɑ̃.z‿aʁ.ʒɑ̃ ɔ̃ nə pø ʁjɛ̃ aʃ.te/
notes: Sans, argent, and on all carry nasal vowels from different families, an, an, and on, inside one short clause.

fr: Leurs parents leur offrent un cadeau.
en: Their parents are giving them a gift.
ipa: /lœʁ pa.ʁɑ̃ lœʁ ɔ.fʁ œ̃ ka.do/
notes: Leur and leurs sound exactly alike; leur stays invariable here because it means to them, while leurs marks the plural possessive.

fr: Le pont traverse un long fleuve calme.
en: The bridge crosses a long, calm river.
ipa: /lə pɔ̃ tʁa.vɛʁs œ̃ lɔ̃ flœv kalm/
notes: Pont and long both use the on nasal sound though spelled ont and ong; the final consonant letters stay silent.

fr: Il fait chaud sous ce grand chapeau.
en: It is hot under this big hat.
ipa: /il fɛ ʃo su sə ɡʁɑ̃ ʃa.po/
notes: Chaud and chapeau both hide the closed o sound behind au and eau, two spellings for the same vowel.

fr: Elle ne peut pas venir car elle a trop de travail.
en: She can't come because she has too much work.
ipa: /ɛl nə pø pa və.niʁ kaʁ ɛl a tʁo də tʁa.vaj/
notes: Peut (can) sounds identical to peu (little) and peux; only the subject elle plus the verb context confirms this spelling.

fr: Elle range son manteau dans l'armoire brune.
en: She puts her coat away in the brown wardrobe.
ipa: /ɛl ʁɑ̃ʒ sɔ̃ mɑ̃.to dɑ̃ laʁ.mwaʁ bʁyn/
notes: Range, son, and manteau each contain a nasal vowel, an, on, and an again, that must be spelled with the correct letter combination.

fr: Le vase bleu est vide maintenant.
en: The blue vase is empty now.
ipa: /lə vaz blø ɛ vid mɛ̃.tə.nɑ̃/
notes: Maintenant hides the nasal in sound in main before shifting to the nasal an sound in tenant; both must be heard separately.

fr: Les enfants veulent jouer dehors un peu.
en: The children want to play outside a little.
ipa: /le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ vœl ʒwe də.ɔʁ œ̃ pø/
notes: Veulent uses the open eu sound while peu uses the closed eu sound; the same two letters make different vowels depending on what follows.

fr: Un grand pin pousse dans le jardin.
en: A tall pine tree grows in the garden.
ipa: /œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ pɛ̃ pus dɑ̃ lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃/
notes: Pin (pine tree) is a homophone of pain (bread); both share the exact same in nasal sound despite the very different spelling.

fr: Vingt personnes attendent devant le magasin.
en: Twenty people are waiting in front of the store.
ipa: /vɛ̃ pɛʁ.sɔn a.tɑ̃d də.vɑ̃ lə ma.ɡa.zɛ̃/
notes: Vingt starts with the in nasal sound and ends in a silent consonant cluster, while attendent and devant use the an nasal sound.

fr: Elle a un an de plus que moi.
en: She is one year older than me.
ipa: /ɛl a œ̃.n‿ɑ̃ də plys kə mwa/
notes: An (year) sounds identical to en (a preposition); only the meaning of age tells you to write an here.

fr: Le tableau montre un beau paysage doré.
en: The painting shows a beautiful golden landscape.
ipa: /lə ta.blo mɔ̃tʁ œ̃ bo pe.i.zaʒ dɔ.ʁe/
notes: Tableau and beau both spell the closed o sound with eau, while doré uses a plain é sound at the end; keep the vowel families separate.

fr: Nous avons faim, alors mangeons maintenant.
en: We are hungry, so let's eat now.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ fɛ̃ a.lɔʁ mɑ̃.ʒɔ̃ mɛ̃.tə.nɑ̃/
notes: Faim and maintenant share the in nasal sound while avons and mangeons use the on nasal sound; four nasal vowels appear in one short sentence.

fr: Quand pars-tu en vacances cet été ?
en: When are you leaving on vacation this summer?
ipa: /kɑ̃ paʁ ty ɑ̃ va.kɑ̃s sɛ.t‿e.te/
notes: Quand (when) is a homophone of quant and qu'en; here the question word about time is required.

fr: Les amis arrivent en avance ce soir.
en: The friends are arriving early tonight.
ipa: /le.z‿a.mi a.ʁiv ɑ̃.n‿a.vɑ̃s sə swaʁ/
notes: Les amis and en avance both require a liaison sound linking to the next word's vowel; the linking consonant is never written onto the first word.

fr: Ils peuvent venir dès qu'ils veulent.
en: They can come as soon as they want.
ipa: /il pœv və.niʁ dɛ kil vœl/
notes: Dès (as soon as) sounds like des, the plural article; here dès signals timing, not quantity.
